title: Impact of Mobile Phone Coverage on Market Prices

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Two-Stage Least Squares (Instrumental Variables).  

Why IV?  
• Treatment (mobile adoption x) is potentially endogenous – regions that adopt mobile coverage early may differ systematically (e.g., richer, better connected).  
• We observe a plausible instrument z: topographic suitability for installing base stations. Terrain is largely predetermined, affects the cost / feasibility of network roll-out (relevance), and—conditional on controls—should not directly shift market prices except through mobile phone adoption (exclusion).  

Key assumptions  
1. Relevance: Cov(z, x) ≠ 0 (terrain strongly predicts mobile adoption).  
2. Exclusion / exogeneity: E[ z · u ] = 0, where u is the structural error in the price equation—i.e., conditional on controls, topography influences prices only through mobile adoption.  
3. Monotonicity (for LATE interpretation): topographic suitability does not decrease the probability of adoption for any unit.  

If these hold, the 2SLS coefficient on x identifies the causal effect of mobile adoption on market prices.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Required packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(AER)          # ivreg
  library(lmtest)       # coeftest
  library(sandwich)     # robust vcov
})

# 1. Read data -------------------------------------------------------------
dat <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s76_data.csv")

# 2. Baseline OLS (naïve) --------------------------------------------------
ols_mod <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = dat)
ols_res  <- coeftest(ols_mod, vcov = vcovHC(ols_mod, type = "HC1"))

# 3. Two-Stage Least Squares ----------------------------------------------
iv_mod <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = dat)

# Robust (HC1) standard errors
iv_res <- coeftest(iv_mod, vcov = vcovHC(iv_mod, type = "HC1"))

# 4. First-stage diagnostics ----------------------------------------------
first_stage <- summary(lm(x ~ z + controls, data = dat))
fs_F <- first_stage$fstatistic[1]           # first-stage F-statistic

# 5. Weak-instrument and over-id tests ------------------------------------
iv_sum <- summary(iv_mod, diagnostics = TRUE)   # reports Wu–Hausman & Sargan

# 6. Print key results -----------------------------------------------------
cat("=== Naïve OLS (robust se) ===\n")
print(ols_res["x", ])

cat("\n=== 2SLS / IV estimate (robust se) ===\n")
print(iv_res["x", ])

cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic on instrument z: ", round(fs_F, 2), "\n")
cat("\n--- Instrument diagnostics ---\n")
print(iv_sum$diagnostics)

# 7. Robustness check: add quadratic control ------------------------------
iv_mod_quad <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + I(controls^2) |
                         z + controls + I(controls^2),
                     data = dat)
iv_quad_res <- coeftest(iv_mod_quad,
                        vcov = vcovHC(iv_mod_quad, type = "HC1"))
cat("\n=== 2SLS with quadratic control (robust se) ===\n")
print(iv_quad_res["x", ])
```

Running this script will:  
• read the provided CSV;  
• report the naïve OLS and IV coefficients for mobile adoption;  
• give robust standard errors, the first-stage F-statistic, Wu–Hausman endogeneity test, and Sargan over-identification test;  
• present one robustness specification adding a quadratic term in the control.

## 3. Expected Findings  
Economic intuition: Wider mobile phone coverage reduces information frictions, narrowing spatial price dispersion and curbing opportunistic mark-ups, so the net effect on observed market prices (y) should be negative.  

Magnitude: With the variables standardized (mean ≈ 0, sd ≈ 1), a one-standard-deviation increase in mobile adoption is expected to lower prices by roughly 0.20–0.35 standard deviations (i.e., IV coefficient in the range −0.20 to −0.35). The OLS estimate will likely be smaller in absolute value (closer to zero) if better-off regions both adopt mobile phones and face higher equilibrium prices, creating upward endogeneity bias that IV corrects downward.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use topographic suitability as an instrument for mobile adoption.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased mobile adoption leads to a decrease in market prices.
